A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DecompGAIL with the same authors, core framework and WOMD evaluation. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original traffic-simulation results, including training-stability experiments, DecompGAIL benchmark performance, component ablations and qualitative rollouts.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds parameter sweeps, gradient-penalty comparisons, a map-encoder ablation and success/failure analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Algorithm 1 add a BC loss to the stated PPO fine-tuning objective; v1's update specifies PPO surrogate and value losses only. The SMART backbone, discriminator decomposition and social-reward construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate WOMD traffic simulation with the same participant types and task requirements. The new parameter studies and rollout cases examine the retained task without establishing additional dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LLM2AD while retaining all previous baselines. New Table 4 evaluates WGAN-GP, R1 and R2 variants of PS-GAIL and DecompGAIL, substantially expanding the comparison with alternative approaches to discriminator stabilization.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes interaction-weight parameters (alpha, beta) from (1, 10) to (10, 2.5), and social-reward parameters from (1, 10) to (1, 2.5). New experiments introduce parameter sweeps, penalty controls and encoder freezing/unfreezing. Dataset splits, rollout settings and training budgets remain unchanged; the reported parameter revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's stability and component ablations, v2 adds weighting sensitivity analysis (Section 5.5), gradient-penalty tests (Appendix B), a map-encoder freezing control (Appendix C), and four successful/failing rollout analyses (Appendix G). These substantially broaden examination of design choices and failure behavior.

E5.justification: Mean discriminator scores with standard-deviation shading already appear in v1's Figure 3. v2 retains this reporting and uses the same convention in Figure 6, without introducing seed counts, repeated-training information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1 and 2 remain numerically unchanged. v2 adds LLM2AD results, including the best listed minADE of 1.2827, parameter-sweep scores, encoder-training findings and failure cases. New Table 4 reports PS-GAIL at 0.7674 and PS-GAIL + R1 at 0.7776, versus DecompGAIL at 0.7889. These are additional comparisons, not demonstrated improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The Markov-game definitions and mathematical content of Equations 1–11 are retained. Neither version provides formal proofs, and the new empirical analyses introduce no additional theoretical derivations or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: identifying irrelevant interaction misguidance, addressing it through decomposed discrimination and social PPO, improving stability, and achieving state-of-the-art WOSAC realism.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of sensitivity to neighborhood weighting and why gradient smoothing may impair collision/off-road discrimination. Appendix G interprets behavioral diversity and explicitly documents collision and off-road failures despite appropriate discriminator responses, adding qualifications to the retained realism narrative.

D1.justification: v2 revises weighting hyperparameters in Table 3 and specifies a penalty weight of 1 for the new regularization experiments. The relocated reproducibility statement removes v1's future code-release commitment. Hardware, training times, optimizer settings and CAT-K access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting existing discussion, including Brown et al., Kuefler et al., Mescheder et al. and LLM2AD, and replaces the Chao survey citation with Pan et al. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged; publication updates and consolidated duplicate references do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. Local edits clarify the ego-agent terminology, reorganize baseline categories into bullets, standardize citations and update publication metadata. A hyperparameter subsection and appendix sections are inserted, while the reproducibility statement moves from Section 7 to Appendix F.

P2.justification: v2 adds sensitivity heatmaps (Figure 4), encoder-training curves (Figure 6), four realism-score case figures (Figures 7–10), and the regularization comparison table (Table 4). Table 1 gains a comparator row. v1's qualitative Figure 4 is retained as Figure 5, rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added regularization controls, sensitivity analysis and explicit failure cases improve scrutiny of the design and supplement v1's existing benchmark and ablation evidence. The overall gain is limited by reporting ambiguities: the added BC loss lacks a specified mixing weight, and Section 5.5 lists a social-reward scale of 5 where Figure 4 labels the corresponding row 2.
